title: Rock and roll, rhythm and blues and swing
summary: Early rock and roll and R&B as swing music, and his loss of interest once it went to an eight-beat feel.

bands.name: Louis Jordan and His Tympany Five

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You know you mentioned Buddy Holly, and that era of rock & roll. When I listen to that music, in fact I play a lot of it now, a lot of it’s basically swing music.
Right? “Rock Around the Clock” is a swing song.
Um hum. It doesn’t have an eight beat feel.

I didn’t want to be — I mean rhythm & blues was nice, you know, Louis Jordan and the Tympani Five. That was something that was sitting on the dining room table. I can’t remember all the names of the tunes, I’ve still got them there. But I mean that was Earl Bostic, all of those were swing music. But when it went into eight beat, when it started becoming [scats] that’s when I kind of lost interest in it.
